name: Natural testosterone optimization routine

card.summary: A lifestyle, diet and supplement routine aimed at raising testosterone to support muscle, leanness and a more masculine look.
card.note: Low testosterone symptoms warrant a clinician's assessment.

quick.overview:
The natural testosterone optimization routine is a set of lifestyle habits people use hoping to raise testosterone without prescription hormones. Typical elements are resistance training, sleep, body-weight management and diet.

The appearance payoff is claimed through more muscle, less fat and masculine features. Testosterone levels fall gradually with age, per Wikipedia, which motivates much of the interest.
quick.how: Forum users discuss lifting heavy, short rest periods, sleeping well, eating enough dietary fat and cholesterol such as eggs, and keeping vitamin and mineral intake adequate. Effects are usually judged by how users feel or by blood tests.
quick.risks: Wikipedia notes that zinc over-supplementation does not change serum testosterone and that evidence on low-fat diets is limited. Some forum tips, such as drinking raw eggs, carry food-safety concerns. Low testosterone symptoms can have medical causes.

lead: The natural testosterone optimization routine, also called natural T boosting, is a bundle of lifestyle and supplement practices intended to raise or maintain testosterone levels without prescription therapy. [1][2]

Proponents link higher testosterone to muscle growth, lower body fat and a more masculine appearance, and discuss it in the context of training and diet. [1][3] Wikipedia describes how levels gradually decline with age and how factors such as resistance training, sleep and weight influence them. [2]

chain: More muscle, less fat and a more masculine physique
angle.text: Practitioners aim to support the hormone that drives muscle and leanness. The routine is therefore pursued as part of physique building.

paras: A looksmax.org post argues that cholesterol is the raw material for testosterone and suggests increasing dietary cholesterol, with replies describing eating several eggs daily. [1]
T Nation members discuss rest periods between sets, with one recalling a conference session that said 3x10 with one minute of rest boosted testosterone and growth hormone. [3]

Wikipedia states that resistance training raises testosterone acutely, REM sleep raises nighttime levels, weight loss may raise levels since fat tissue contains aromatase, and vitamin D at 400-1000 IU/day is reported to raise levels. It says zinc deficiency lowers levels but extra zinc does not change serum testosterone. [2]
No studies found for the routine as a whole. Individual factors such as exercise, sleep and nutrients have been studied separately and are summarized in general references. [2]

lore.intro: Looksmax.org and T Nation discuss food, training and sleep tactics for testosterone. [1][3]

claims.believers: A post argues cholesterol is the precursor of testosterone and recommends eggs; replies say they eat several daily. [1]
claims.experts: Wikipedia lists vitamin A, vitamin D and zinc status as factors and describes evidence on low-fat diets as limited; it does not report dietary cholesterol as a lever. [2]

claims.claim: Short rest between sets boosts testosterone.
claims.believers: A T Nation user recalls a conference session recommending 3x10 with 60-second rests. [3]
claims.experts: Wikipedia reports that resistance training raises testosterone acutely. [2]
